---
title: "JavaScript API"
subtitle: "Control Veil from the page."
description: "Show, hide, and toggle groups, set the level, apply a state, and listen for changes with the Veil object."
---

## The Veil object

Veil adds `window.Veil` to every page that has veiled content.

```js
window.Veil = {
  show(group),
  hide(group),
  toggle(group),
  setLevel(level),
  apply(state),
  state()
};
```

| Method | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `show(group)` | Shows the group. On a ladder group, it raises the setting if needed. |
| `hide(group)` | Hides the group. On a ladder group, it lowers the setting if needed. |
| `toggle(group)` | Shows the group if it is hidden, else hides it. |
| `setLevel(level)` | Sets the ladder setting. |
| `apply(state)` | Applies a string in the [state grammar](state.qmd#grammar). |
| `state()` | Returns the current state. |

: Methods of `window.Veil`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[25,75]"}

`state()` returns `{ level, groups, text }`.

- `level` is the ladder setting, or `null` when there is no ladder.
- `groups` is an object from independent group name to a boolean.
- `text` is the full state in the state grammar.

If the document has no veiled element, the calls do nothing.
`state()` then returns `{ level: null, groups: {}, text: '' }`.

## Events

Each change sends a `veil:change` event on `document`.
The `detail` of the event is the same object that `state()` returns.

```js
document.addEventListener('veil:change', function (event) {
  console.log(event.detail.text);
});
```

## Example

```js
Veil.setLevel(2);
Veil.hide('backup');
Veil.apply('level:1,-backup');
```

Each call that changes the state updates the URL, shows the toast, and sends the event.
There are two exceptions.

- Veil refuses a state that hides every slide of a Reveal.js deck.
  Veil writes a message in the browser console, and the state does not change.
- With `toast: false`, there is no toast.
